title: Find Me the Worst Possible Place: Paul Farmer at Rwinkwavu
conflicts: Staffing at Rwinkwavu: the Boston Globe (2008) says 'no staff', PIH's January 2007 update says a handful of overworked nurses, and 2015 staff recollections say no doctor and too few nurses; the story uses the agreed no-doctor point and PIH's handful of nurses. Beds: 96 (Globe, April 2008) vs 110 (Bill Frist, 2014); the story uses the dated 2008 figure.
notes: Different episode from the existing Cange/Haiti edition (PIH's first African site, chosen November 2004, opened summer 2005); the repeat screen flags it as same-founder but lets it through. Founder field is Paul Farmer only, because no source documents a role for Ophelia Dahl in this episode. Company field written 'Inshuti Mu Buzima (PIH)' because the repeat screen matched the word 'Health' against Indus Hospital & Health Network (a different organisation); noted in research_notes. Farmer's own account comes from his May 2012 MIT OpenCourseWare lecture transcript. PIH pages 403 for the verifier, so they are cited as Internet Archive copies, which load intermittently from this machine; the Globe, MIT OCW, Globe 2022 and Frist pages load reliably.
